transcript:
Meeting: Arbor Tech Systems — Redwood quickstart & hosting discussion
Date: 2026-03-14 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE); Jules Kwan (Redwood SE); Maya Chen (Arbor CTO); Tom Alvarez (Infra); Priya Singh (Product)
---
Summary:
- Customer evaluating Redwood for in-product assistant (autocomplete + private data search). Interested in PLG/self-serve path but needs clarity on time-to-first-token, free credits, and whether to start Hosted or jump to Dedicated/Private due to data residency concerns.
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS mentioned; likely to require Private for regulated subset of customers.
- Next: Samir to send quickstart and credits instructions; Jules to run cost/latency estimate for 200 qps prototype.
---
Topics: Quickstart flow, free credits, time-to-first-token (TTFT), Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, VPC/KMS, latency vs cost tradeoffs, rollout plan for canary/metrics.
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thank you for carving out time. I'm Samir, AE at Redwood, and with me is Jules, our SE. How are you doing, Maya?
[00:08] Maya: Good, thanks. Excited to get into this — we've got a small scoping team here. Tom and Priya on the line.
[00:13] Tom: hey.
[00:14] Priya: hi all.
[00:17] Samir: Cool. The agenda I sent earlier — quick intro, your goals, TTFT and credits, then hosting fit. We can go deep on latency/cost after that. Sound good?
[00:26] Priya: yep, that's right. Our immediate thing is time-to-first-token — we wanna get a prototype in a week or so. free credits would help.
[00:34] Maya: and we need to know whether we can start hosted and then move to private without rewriting code.
[00:40] Jules: Absolutely — seamless migration is a big focus. Usually teams do hosted first (fastest TTFT), then Dedicated when they need throughput or private for data residency. We support the same API across all three.
[00:50] Maya: what's the typical onramp? like, how many hours to first call?
[00:54] Samir: it can be literally minutes if you're doing a dev prototype — create API key, run the quickstart curl/SDK. With our free credits we can give you X tokens to burn through. Then for a small app, TTFT = same day. For a production workload with SSO/KMS and VPC we'll usually factor in a couple weeks for network setup and security review.
[01:15] Tom: couple questions — latency for autocomplete is sensitive. We're targeting 100–200 ms p95. Is that realistic on Hosted?
[01:24] Jules: Depends on model and sequence length. For smaller models and tuned batching, Hosted in a nearby region can hit sub-150ms p95 for single-turn short completions. If you need consistent 100ms at 200 qps, Dedicated with reserved GPU pools is more predictable. Also quantized model variants help.
[01:42] Maya: ok. And about costs — we're optimizing cost per 1k tokens. How do we balance that with latency?
[01:49] Jules: typical levers: batching (higher throughput reduces tokens/sec cost), prefix caching for repeated prompts, and switching to quantized variants. We'll model that for your 200 qps example.
[01:58] Priya: does Redwood do KV cache or prefix cache? I heard you mention KV earlier in your docs.
[02:03] Jules: yes, we have prefix/KV cache. Sorry if the auto transcription on that doc said "KV cash" once — it's cache. It reduces repeated token generation when users re-query similar context.
[02:12] Tom: haha ok good.
[02:14] Maya: security — we are regulated for parts of our business. We need SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS-managed keys. Also audit logs for requests. Is that supported?
[02:25] Samir: yes. Hosted offers SOC2 and enterprise SSO integrations; Dedicated gives you stricter network isolation and support contracts; Private (VPC/on-prem) lets you plug in your KMS/HSM and keeps the control plane customer-managed. We maintain audit logs in all tiers, but Private gives you the option to keep them inside your environment.
[02:45] Maya: great. Any gotchas on moving from Hosted to Private? e.g., API changes, data migration, or vendor lock-in?
[02:52] Jules: API is the same. The main work is network and identity—setting up the Private control plane, VPN or direct connect, and KMS integration. You might need to roll model weights in your environment if you want air-gapped. But code changes in app layer are minimal.
[03:08] Priya: perfect. For the free credits — how many tokens, and what's the process to get them?
[03:13] Samir: We usually issue a pilot credit pack; for quickstarts it's enough for several thousand requests. I'll send the activation link — you can apply the credits to your account and they're visible in the console.
[03:22] Maya: can we restrict which team members get keys?
[03:26] Samir: yes, RBAC in the console and fine-grained API keys per project.
[03:30] Tom: network-wise, we have a VPC with strict egress rules. If we start hosted, we need to know allowed IP ranges and whether outbound to Redwood is accepted.
[03:39] Jules: we publish egress endpoints and recommend using a short list of region endpoints; for higher security you can set up a reverse proxy. For Dedicated/Private we can do peering or direct connect.
[03:50] Maya: do you support per-tenant data separation? Some of our customers want dedicated data paths.
[03:56] Jules: Dedicated can be scoped by customer tenant in the serving layer; Private of course gives you total separation. We'll capture specific requirements in the pilot scope.
[04:04] Priya: timeline question again — if we want to demo to internal stakeholders in 7 days, is that feasible?
[04:09] Samir: Yes. Steps: 1) sign-up, 2) I send credits and quickstart link, 3) spin up a prototype using SDK or curl, 4) run a few sample prompts. If you want low-latency region selection we'll advise which model/region combo. That can be done in a day or two.
[04:25] Tom: okay. about throughput — if we go to 200 qps in pilot, do you recommend Hosted bursting or reserve Dedicated capacity?
[04:33] Jules: For a short pilot, Hosted with burst capacity is fine; for sustained 200 qps, Dedicated gives predictable SLOs and lower unit cost. We'll simulate both in the estimate.
[04:42] Maya: is there a sample benchmark you can run for us? We can share a small prompt set and some logs.
[04:47] Jules: absolutely — please upload a redacted prompt sample and we'll run a mini benchmark. Note the benchmarking should include realistic payloads and sequence lengths.
[04:56] Priya: any compliance docs we can review ahead of legal?
[04:59] Samir: I'll include SOC2 and the security pack link. Also the Private deployment checklist if you need air-gap.
[05:07] Maya: curious about cost numbers in concrete terms — could you give a rough hosted vs dedicated cost for our 200 qps scenario?
[05:15] Jules: rough back-of-envelope: if you use a mid-size quantized model for short completions, Hosted might run $X–Y per 1M tokens depending on batching; Dedicated gives discounts at commit rates. I'll produce a spreadsheet with assumptions.
[05:27] Tom: we also use internal embeddings for search. Are embeddings supported? storage? retention?
[05:33] Jules: yes, embeddings supported via the same API. For storage/retention, you can elect to have us not retain requests (no retention) for Dedicated/Private, or set retention windows on Hosted. We'll capture retention policy in the pilot.
[05:46] Maya: last technical question — how do you handle model fallbacks if a model is overloaded? We need graceful degradation.
[05:53] Jules: smart routing: requests route by policy, and we can fallback to lower-capacity compatible variants. For critical paths you can set automatic fallback rules to avoid failures.
[06:02] Priya: that sounds good.
[06:04] Samir: ok, quick recap of next steps: I'll send the quickstart + credits and the security pack; Jules will run the latency/cost estimate and a small benchmark if you share prompts; Maya to confirm PII needs and whether pilot must be VPC/private. Any additional items?
[06:19] Maya: could you also include a sample rollout plan for canary + A/B? stakeholders want to see progress gating.
[06:25] Samir: yes, will include a 2-week pilot runway doc with canary checks and metrics.
[06:29] Tom: thanks.
[06:30] Samir: great. We'll follow up in the next few days. Thanks everyone.
[06:34] [END]
